rounds.text: Praruh Technologies Ltd presents severe fundamental and operational risks that undermine its seemingly attractive headline multiples, starting with an alarming disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation [E24]. Specifically, cash conversion stands at a concerning 0.00x for Mar 2026, with operating cash flow coming in at Rs 0 Cr and free cash flow dropping to negative Rs -1 Cr [E24, E25, E26]. Operating cash flow represents a mere 19% of operating profit, exposing a heavy reliance on accruals and signalling that reported earnings are not translating into hard cash [E24, E27]. This cash generation deficit is further compounded by extreme working capital pressures, evidenced by dangerously high debtors of 273 days and a ballooning of working capital days from 29.4 days to 84.8 days [E43, E44]. Operational stability is also questionable, with both yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends flagged as inconsistent over recent periods [E22, E23]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company stubbornly refuses to reward shareholders, paying a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E42]. Conceded: the company boasts a pristine debt-free balance sheet with borrowings at zero, strong multi-year sales and profit growth, and high trailing returns on capital [E10, E14, E16, E29, E40].
